task.assignment: Downtown — the programs that hold the block and the people who founded them
task.approach: Neighborhood approach: this slice is one block's record — its community programs and their founders, who is moving in or out, who the block has in a hospital bed or in custody, what it paid on tax day, whose debts crossed the line, and the engine's neighborhood hooks this cycle. First-person witness, one block one truth. The programs, founders, movement numbers, patients, defendants and money lines are real; the stoop conversations, the mailboxes, the dog everyone knows are yours. Facts on this slice: the names, places, roles and numbers listed. Those are real; do not invent people or places. Everything else about this beat — what it looks like, who is there, what they want and hate — is yours to paint.

plan.focus: The tension between Downtown's institutional stability (NeuroCity) and its fragile human margins.
plan.closeQuestion: Is the stability of the block's programs enough to offset the individual collapses of its residents?

sources.name: Ryan Stark
sources.quote: I walked by SpeedyBurger on Broadway and saw a new lease sign go up above it. The paper was still crisp in the display case. It's another new spot opening up in Downtown, which is great to see.

sources.name: Gordon Tate
sources.quote: I just noticed another new spot opening up around Downtown. It's always something new popping up, which is fine, but with the rent going up the way it is, you start wondering who these places are actually for.

sources.name: Carlos Presti
sources.quote: I saw another new spot opening up Downtown. I don't know what it is yet, but I'm always curious to see what actually sticks around here. It's just good to see something new moving in.

sources.name: Lucia Polito
sources.quote: I heard about Downtown First Friday Live Music last night, and it made me think about how vibrant Downtown can be. It's great to see people coming together for events like that.
